# Finite schedules of batches and compaction

Start from an actual stored prefix state with its structural `WellFormed`
invariant and retained root. Each action is either an actual finite batch of
rooted keyed occurrences or an actual compaction. The schedule executes the
existing batch step or compactor through a chronological `List.foldl` on the
existing state fiber carrying these proofs. It introduces no replacement
state, path or desired decoding axiom.

Erasing compaction actions gives a chronological list of batches. The actual
checked decoder of the schedule equals that of the existing batch runner on
this projected list. Root, complete typed histories, keys, order and
multiplicity are retained. Decidable equality of full typed edge tags is
explicit; criteria for new rows remain separate evidence obligations.

## Partial retention and reintroduced payloads

The checked fixture starts with dictionary `[[F], [], [P]]` and two real
references to slot `0`. The first actual compaction produces `[[], [F]]`,
remapping `F: 0 → 1` and dropping the unused `P` at old slot `2`. A genuine
batch then appends a parallel `P` history. A second actual compaction produces
`[[F], [], [P]]` with real references `[(11, 0), (11, 0), (12, 2)]` and full
histories `F, F, P`.

The original and final dictionaries coincide, and direct lookup of the old
`P` payload in the final dictionary returns `some 2`. Composition of the actual
partial retention maps remains `none`: the first compaction dropped it.
The positive module proves these actual producer and lookup equations before
the negative control rejects direct lookup as composed-remap evidence.
Empty schedules, repeated compactions, internal empty batches, repeated keys,
chronological histories and distinct retained roots have positive controls.
A general cumulative numeric transport theorem for old real references remains
open; these semantic schedule results do not assert total remaps on unused slots.

## Verification and limits

The [source](../../../../GRWTSK/Combinatorics/DirectedGraph/PrefixTableSchedule.lean),
[positive controls](../../../../GRWTSK/Combinatorics/DirectedGraph/Checks/Positive/PrefixTableSchedule.lean),
[native receipt](../../../../evidence/Combinatorics/DirectedGraph/prefix-compaction-schedule-checks-2026-10-15.json)
and [integration record](../../../../evidence/Combinatorics/DirectedGraph/prefix-compaction-schedule-integration-2026-10-15.json)
bind the fresh selected closure and controls. Pinned Lean 4.33.0 checks trust
zero, fatal warnings and every owned declaration and transitive axiom,
allowing only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Clean pinned
dependency objects are reused and fingerprinted; their sources and the whole
umbrella are not rebuilt.

The [durable decision](../../../../cache/decisions/compaction-schedule-state-v1.json)
separates semantic history preservation, slot retention and payload lookup.
This does not supply raw array stability, automatic criteria or an operational
parser/JSON/hash/compression/filesystem/transaction refinement. Local source
is MIT; named imported Lean/Mathlib contributors retain their individual
credits and terms. Human direction: R.A. Jacob Martone; formalization/checking:
OpenAI Codex. Correlated model/source review is not independent validation.

# Cubic-root reduction in the third cyclotomic integer ring

Use the actual field $K=\operatorname{CyclotomicField}(3,\mathbb Q)$ and its
[ring of integers](third-cyclotomic-ideals.md) $O$. Define the original source's
$\omega$ by `(IsCyclotomicExtension.zeta_spec 3 ℚ K).toInteger` and
$\lambda=\omega-1$. Then $\omega$ is a primitive cube root in $O$.

For an actual maximal ideal $P$ of $O$, the exact good-prime hypothesis
$\lambda\notin P$ implies that the actual quotient image of $\omega$ is a
primitive cube root in $O/P$. The proof uses the actual quotient field and
original root, with the exclusion retained explicitly.

## Actual ramified ideal and controls

The actual ideal $I=(\lambda)$ is prime, nonzero, maximal and proper, with
$N(I)=3$ and $|O/I|=3$. It contains $\lambda$ and $3$, and excludes $2$.
The image of $\omega$ in this quotient equals $1$ and fails to be a primitive
cube root. Thus maximality alone cannot supply the good-prime exclusion.
The intended negative control rejects precisely that substitution.

The good-prime theorem has a genuine consumer: the norm $N((2))=4$ makes
$(2)$ proper. A maximal ideal $P$ containing it exists. If $\lambda\in P$,
then $3,2\in P$ force $1\in P$, a contradiction. Consequently there is an
actual maximal $P$ above $(2)$ with $\lambda\notin P$, where the quotient
image of $\omega$ has order $3$. This does not identify $(2)$ itself as maximal
or its quotient as a particular finite field.

There is also no $p\in O$ satisfying both $I=(p)$ and
$\lambda^2\mid p-1$. Those conditions would put $p$ and $p-1$ in the proper
ideal $I$, forcing $1\in I$. The literal generator $p=\lambda$ is a checked
instance. Existence of a normalized generator at good primes remains a
separate obligation.

## Sources, verification and remaining suppliers

The [source](../../../../GRWTSK/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/ThirdCyclotomicReduction.lean),
[positive controls](../../../../GRWTSK/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Checks/Positive/ThirdCyclotomicReduction.lean),
[native receipt](../../../../evidence/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/third-cyclotomic-reduction-checks-2026-10-15.json)
and [integration record](../../../../evidence/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/third-cyclotomic-reduction-integration-2026-10-15.json)
bind fresh selected sources and actual controls. Pinned Lean 4.33.0 checks trust
zero, fatal warnings and every owned declaration and transitive axiom,
allowing only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Clean pinned
dependency objects are reused and fingerprinted; their sources and the whole
umbrella are not rebuilt.

The actual root definitions and reduction proof retain OpenAI project credit
and Apache-2.0 terms from
[FiniteFourier](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/lean/OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/GaussSum/FiniteFourier.lean).
Mathlib's cyclotomic ideal results retain Xavier Roblot's named credit, with
individual imported cyclotomic/number-field/ideal-norm credits including
Riccardo Brasca, Ashvni Narayanan, Anne Baanen, Alex J. Best and Eric Rodriguez. The
[source review](../../../../evidence/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/third-cyclotomic-reduction-source-review-2026-10-15.json)
records exact identities and bounded source comparisons. Human direction:
R.A. Jacob Martone; adaptation, formalization and checking: OpenAI Codex.
Correlated model/source review is not independent validation.

Original cubic/sextic characters, Jacobi and normalized primary-generator
witnesses, Gauss coefficients, cube/column and Möbius weights, corrected masks,
completed ideal sums and common support for every frequency remain open.
These local root-reduction results do not close finite completed-sum
interchange, global bounds, the original detector or RH. They establish no
operational cache refinement.
